quote: The pattern itself, a network of particle streams built by vision-cone attraction, is documented.
reason: States the stream network is documented and only the numbers (fractal dimension, void scaling, junction counts) are missing.

quote: I found no source that describes this exact nematic (2θ) system or the four-defect splitting of a +1 defect.
reason: States the four-defect splitting of +1 defects was not found, and the nematic +1/2 propulsion has no direct source and is only expected.

quote: The model and its ordered phase are described in the literature. I could not verify the specific two-stage coarsening numbers, namely the early exponent of 0.5, the crossover near t≈1000 and the late exponent of 0.34.
reason: Frames the gap as numbers, says the two-stage pattern is qualitatively in Mahapatra et al. and the papers 'probably cover this', though it lists early-domain dissolution among unconfirmed items.

quote: I didn't find any paper on this exact model (a noisy voter model with its average opinion reset to 0.3), but each part of the behaviour is documented.
reason: What is missing is the exact model and phase diagram; it says each part of the behaviour and multi-peak distributions under external influence are documented and the three peaks are expected.

quote: One specific twist in what the stripes do, which goes beyond the rule choice, is something I couldn't find described anywhere.
reason: States the opposite-travelling lanes of band trains in the standard single-species Vicsek model are not described anywhere.

quote: What I couldn't find in print is the specific reading your simulation suggests. That reading is magnetisation falling to zero as a power of ln L, with an exponent proportional to temperature
reason: Says logarithmic scaling at sigma=2 is documented (read as true order), but the power-of-log decay with no long-range order, the central feature, is stated as not in print.

quote: The mechanism and the gas–dense coexistence are firmly documented for inertial spinners.
reason: Treats torque-driven inertial phase separation as published (disk RIPS); what is missing is the dumbbell shape, the hexatic dense phase and the 1/3 exponent, which are rule details or secondary features.

quote: One dense blob persists alongside the travelling bands, rather than the bands breaking up into an array of aggregates.
reason: Says the ingredients and structures are documented, but lists blob-band coexistence as phenomenology it could not find described.

quote: The ring and ABP-polymer compaction, the non-monotonic size, and the re-swelling at high Pe are all well documented.
reason: States collapse and re-swelling are documented; only the J-dependence and N-independence are missing.

quote: At T=0.07, pair bonds and triangle bonds start rising at the same time, and the system goes straight from gas to lattice. The literature mostly reports two steps instead: a disordered network forms first, then reorganises.
reason: Kagome assembly is called documented, but the one-step gas-to-lattice nucleation, the central reported feature, is stated as not described (literature reports two-step).

quote: The core behaviour is documented: a chain with no attraction collapses when its beads self-propel, inertia changes where that happens, and the chain swells back at high activity.
reason: States the core collapse/re-swelling behaviour is documented; the ring is a rule-combination gap and the exponent is a suspect detail.

quote: Twist not found: phase-dependent splitting of a +1 defect into four defects (likely 3x(+1/2)+1x(-1/2)), with onset near s~0.15 and 64% of phases at s=0.5, in a nematic (cos2phi) non-reciprocal kernel model
reason: Treats +1/2 propulsion as documented or expected, but states the +1 to four-defect splitting, half of the reported behaviour, was not found.

quote: The behaviour itself, side-by-side lanes of travelling polar clusters moving in opposite directions, is documented for the kinetic (Boltzmann-equation) version of Vicsek-style polar alignment.
reason: Says the lane behaviour is documented in an equivalent kinetic theory and 'isn't a new phenomenon'; what is missing is a particle-level report, which the reported behaviour does emphasise.

quote: Finite-N endgame statistics not found: end states restricted to equal groups whose size divides N; prime N almost always fully synchronizes; full-sync probability jumps around with N; even-N failure falls as about 0.6/N.
reason: Although it calls the core clustering documented and the gap 'not a new kind of behaviour', it states the prime/divisor-dependent finite-N endgame (the central feature) was not found.

quote: Here there is no inoculum: the noisy uniform state breaks up by itself into travelling bands, and these coexist with a single long-lived dense blob on a periodic domain.
reason: Calls the phenomena well documented, but its 'twist not found' explicitly includes bands coexisting with a long-lived dense blob, the central feature.

quote: A diffusive early regime followed by slower coarsening is what the 2020 paper describes.
reason: Concludes the behaviour is documented and the two-regime coarsening is described; the unconfirmed crossover with domain dissolution is treated as effective exponents that probably don't matter.

quote: I did not find the finite-N result you observed: final groupings that are equal-sized and tied to the divisors of N, with full-sync probability depending on N's factorisation.
reason: States that the factorisation-dependent sync probability and divisor-structured final groupings were not found; only the model and large-N doubling are documented.

quote: The shock-induced third peak at the reset value 0.3 and the 6-regime map were not found in the literature; the third peak is the expected result of resetting competing with slow consensus formation.
reason: States the shock-induced third peak (the trimodal behaviour) was not found, adding only that it is expected.

quote: The one new piece is that a +1 defect splits into four defects above s ≈ 0.15, depending on the texture phase. I couldn't find that described anywhere, but it isn't enough to call the whole result undocumented.
reason: Says most of the behaviour is documented but explicitly states the four-defect splitting, a central part of the reported behaviour, is not described.

quote: So the phenomenology isn't new. What it does is take a side in a live interpretive dispute.
reason: Says the power-of-inverse-log decay is documented in an equivalent effective theory, leaving only the absence of an explicit fit for this model.

quote: These look like new measurements of a known pattern rather than a new behaviour.
reason: States the stream-network behaviour is documented and the gap is only quantitative network-shape measurements.

quote: Not found: final states as m equal clusters for each divisor m of N (9 at N=100), prime-N near-certain sync with only the all-separate state as alternative, and the ~0.6/N even-N failure law.
reason: Says equal-sized cluster states and failure of sync are known, but the prime/divisor structure of sync probability, the central feature, is listed as not found.

quote: The behaviour is a documented model plus a documented general mechanism.
reason: Says the outcome follows from documented pieces and is 'not a new phenomenon'; not-found items are the model combination and the regime count, though it warns other trimodal papers do not describe this behaviour.

quote: Is the behaviour already described? Yes, in the same model class.
reason: Answers that the behaviour is described ('leaning KNOWN'), though it admits the 2D blob-plus-bands coexistence is expected rather than directly confirmed.

quote: The behaviour itself is documented.
reason: Says RIPS is the same behaviour under a different rule; the hexatic dense phase and unarrested coarsening it could not find are treated as secondary twists.

quote: Undocumented twist: final states are exactly m equal clusters for each divisor m of N (9 states at N=100), near-certain sync for prime N, and roughly 0.6/N failure for even N.
reason: Calls the 'main behaviour' (sync not guaranteed, clusters survive) documented but states the divisor/prime-N structure, which is the reported behaviour's core, was not found.

quote: The model family and the qualitative phenomenon (a surface-driven early regime, then coarsening, then macroscopic phase separation) are well documented.
reason: States the qualitative two-stage phenomenon is documented and only exponents/crossover numbers are unconfirmed, with mild doubt whether domain dissolution matches the documented onset.

quote: I am confident that the model class and the qualitative phenomena are known.
reason: Opens by saying no source reports the exact rise-then-fall and spot-stripe-uniform sequence, but concludes the qualitative phenomena (non-monotonic coupling effect, spot/stripe changes) are documented in close relatives, leaving only setup and numbers.

quote: The model class and the collapse-then-reswelling behaviour are clearly documented.
reason: States the behaviour is documented for a linear chain (treated as equivalent); missing items are ring-specific numbers and J-window details.

quote: The size-vs-length exponent of about 0 at J=10 is the only feature I couldn't find in the literature, and it looks more like a numerical artifact than new physics.
reason: Only a non-central exponent is missing; collapse and re-swelling are treated as documented.

quote: I did not find a source that specifically describes direct gas-to-kagome nucleation with the pair-then-triangle timing, so I treat it as likely but unverified.
reason: Calls kagome assembly documented and likens the triangle-first pathway to Chen et al., but concludes direct one-step nucleation from the gas was not found.

quote: I found no source that describes the specific outcome, which is the divisor-structured final groupings and their N-dependent failure rates.
reason: States the divisor-structured outcome and N-dependent failure rates are not described; only the model and marginal-case failure are documented.

quote: But the behaviour you'd predict from the published pieces matches what was observed, so this isn't a discovery.
reason: Concludes both parts are documented and trimodality is not new for the family; only the 6-regime phase diagram is missing.

quote: The behaviour is documented: a chiral fluid driven only by torque splits from a uniform state into a dilute phase and a dense phase.
reason: States the torque-driven phase separation is documented; undocumented items are the coupling mechanism, the (expected) hexatic dense phase, continued coarsening and the onset value.

quote: I found no description of this four-defect outcome, its threshold, or its phase dependence.
reason: Calls the core (+1/2 propulsion) documented but states the +1 to four-defect splitting was not found.

quote: The re-entrant sequence (spots → stripes → spots as the death/birth ratio varies near 0.55) is not documented for this model.
reason: Calls the main spots-stripes-gaps sequence documented, but states the three-body route and the re-entrant spots-stripes-spots sequence, central to the reported behaviour, were not found.

quote: I found no source that reports the specific fractal network pattern.
reason: States the fractal stream-network pattern itself is not described and places the system in a regime prior work has not described.

quote: I also found no source for the four-defect splitting of a +1 defect.
reason: States the four-defect splitting was not found and the nematic +1/2 propulsion has no direct source.

quote: Splitting into a dilute liquid and a dense six-fold (hexatic) state is documented for closely related systems.
reason: States the dilute/hexatic splitting is documented; what it could not find is a combination of rule details and continued coarsening.

quote: I found no report of a space-spanning, fractal, branching stream network with a void-area scaling of R³ and a degree-3 junction majority.
reason: Prior work is said to report clusters, worms, files and filaments, not a space-spanning network, though the headline frames the gap as network statistics.

quote: Each part of the behaviour is described in the light-heavy (LH) model papers. The one thing I couldn't confirm is the exact numbers: a late exponent of about 0.34 (roughly 1/3) and a crossover near t≈1000.
reason: States every part of the behaviour, including early-domain dissolution then slow coarsening, is described and only numbers are missing.

quote: The one new-looking feature is that order comes back at e_a/e_p ≈ 33 and T = 6. I couldn't find that described, and I think it is more likely a numerical artefact than a real effect.
reason: Melting is called documented, but the re-entrant recrystallisation above the passive melting temperature, the central half of the reported behaviour, is stated as not found.

quote: Side-by-side lanes moving in opposite directions are documented in closely related models, but I found no report of them in the standard single-species, continuous-angle Vicsek model.
reason: Related models (four-state Potts, two-species) are treated as different systems, and it states the lanes in the standard Vicsek model were not found.

quote: This rule set is essentially the Barberis & Peruani 2016 model, and a network of streams is a documented feature of that model family.
reason: States the stream network is documented and only the specific measurements are missing.

quote: I found no paper that reports a 2D, cell-conserving, nutrient-resupplied system in which a dense blob coexists with travelling bands that carry aggregates.
reason: States the blob-band coexistence is not reported (in prior work the two structures appear separately); only the ingredients are documented.

quote: I found no source describing the specific state you observed: several side-by-side lanes of opposite-travelling band trains, stable in a single-species Vicsek model.
reason: States the lane state itself is not described in the literature found.

quote: The re-entrant restoration is likely related to known chiral re-entrance but I could not confirm it for this exact model.
reason: Lists re-entrance as resembling other chiral systems it says are not the same, and states the high-activity solid ordered above the passive melting temperature was not found.

quote: The main behaviour (shrinking, then swelling back open as activity rises) is already documented in a model that differs from yours only in using a linear chain instead of a ring.
reason: States the main behaviour is documented in an equivalent linear-chain model; missing items are non-central details.

quote: The specific state is not: side-by-side lanes of band trains moving in opposite directions, lasting for a long time, in the ordinary single-species Vicsek model.
reason: States the counter-propagating lane state is not documented; only the building blocks are.

quote: I also didn't find the specific three-peak picture: a peak at the 0.3 reset value alongside the two consensus peaks.
reason: Although it says both parts and the resetting idea are documented, it explicitly states the three-peak distribution itself was not found.

quote: But the behaviour (nutrient-taxis bands carrying or coexisting with an attractant-driven aggregate) is the same.
reason: States the coexistence behaviour is documented (Marenduzzo et al.); only the setup (no growth, uniform start, periodic box) differs.

quote: At low T and low mu, near-simultaneous growth of pairs and triangles is plausible, but I found no source that tests it.
reason: Kagome is called the documented main finding, but it states that direct one-step nucleation from the gas (zero lag) was not found in any source.

quote: The qualitative result is probably not new, but the specific noise-versus-shock-rate phase diagram might not have been published.
reason: Missing items are the reset protocol (a rule) and the phase diagram; it concludes the qualitative result is probably not new.

quote: So a dumbbell version is something the theory predicts, not a new effect.
reason: Treats disk RIPS as the same behaviour family and the dumbbell version as not new, though it adds it found no paper on frictionless torque-driven dumbbells separating into liquid and hexatic phases.

quote: I found no source that clearly describes side-by-side lanes of stripe trains moving in opposite directions as a stable state.
reason: States the lane state is not described, adding only that it is plausibly a special case of known phenomenology.

quote: What I couldn't find described is how finite systems end up: the specific final cluster states and the failure probabilities.
reason: States the finite-N endgame (equal-group divisor states, prime-N sync, failure law) is not described; only the model and large-N growth are documented.

quote: The one twist I couldn't find described is the four-defect splitting above a threshold.
reason: Says the core behaviour is documented in nearby work but states the four-defect splitting, half the reported behaviour, was not found.

quote: Merging streams and interconnected bands are documented for this exact class of model.
reason: Frames the gap as network statistics with network-like structure partly documented, though it notes the documented interconnected network was only transient.
